rationale: No analog interface; pure digital serial protocol

extraction_strategy.ic_class_applicability_gate_v0_1_62: ic_class='serial_peripheral_protocol' declares LL5 not applicable; emitted as N/A stub (l_doc_taxonomy.na_stub)

signaling_summary: Each SAS phy is a full-duplex differential serial link: a transmit pair (TX+/TX-) and an independent receive pair (RX+/RX-). The transmitter drives differential NRZ; the receiver recovers the clock from the encoded stream (8b10b at <=6 Gbps, 128b150b at 12/22.5 Gbps). Spread-spectrum clocking (SSC) may be applied to reduce EMI. There is no separate forwarded clock wire.
oob_signaling_summary: OOB bursts are low-frequency envelopes of ALIGN primitives, separated by idle periods. COMRESET, COMINIT, and COMWAKE differ only in burst-to-idle ratios.
notes: AHCI is explicitly out of scope for PHY analog characteristics (AHCI 1.3.1 §1.3).
clocking: Embedded clock: the receiver recovers bit/dword timing from the 8b10b or 128b150b encoded serial stream via its CDR. Spread-spectrum clocking (SSC) is optional for EMI reduction.

receiver_specs_canonical.clock_recovery: CDR from the encoded serial stream
receiver_specs_canonical.dword_sync: ALIGN / idle dwords maintain dword synchronization.

oob_signaling.purpose: Low-speed burst patterns to detect attachment and distinguish SAS from SATA; COMSAS identifies a SAS phy.
oob_signaling.speed_negotiation: The Speed Negotiation Window (SNW) sequence negotiates the highest common link rate.

encoding_role_in_analog: SAS uses 8b10b (DC-balanced, running disparity) up to 6 Gbps and 128b150b with a forward error correction capability at 12/22.5 Gbps. The line code provides DC balance and transition density for clock recovery; integrity at the frame level comes from the 32-bit CRC and scrambling, and OOB/SNW handle attachment detection and rate negotiation.
